Notice Regarding California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determinations
Pursuant to CEQA, a "project" is defined as a "whole action" subject to a public agency's discretionary funding or approval that has the potential to either (1) cause a direct physical change in the environment or (2) cause a reasonably foreseeable indirect physical change in the environment. "Projects" include discretionary activity by a public agency, a private activity that receives any public funding, or activities that involve the public agency's issuance of a discretionary approval and is not statutorily or categorically exempt from CEQA. (Pub. Res. Code § 21065.) To the extent that matters listed in this Agenda are considered “projects” under CEQA, their appropriate CEQA determination will be listed below each recommendation. If no CEQA determination is listed, it has been determined that the action does not constitute a “project” under CEQA.
Viewing City Council Meetings
Members of the public may view the City Council meeting live on the City’s website https://www.azusaca.gov/1389/Watch-Meetings-Online, or on Channel 3 (Spectrum). Archived video of recorded meetings is also available on the City website. Your attendance at this public meeting may result in the recording and broadcast of your image and/or voice as previously described.
Procedures for Addressing the Council
The Council encourages interested people to address this legislative body by making public comments. Public comments may be made during designated agendized public comment periods and during public hearing items. Public comments are limited to five (5) minutes per speaker, unless a different time is announced by the Mayor/presiding Chair.
The Council encourages free expression of all points of view. To allow all persons the opportunity to speak, please keep your remarks brief. If others have already expressed your position, you may simply indicate that you agree with a previous speaker. If appropriate, a spokesperson may present the views of your entire group. State law generally prohibits the City Council from responding to or acting upon matters not listed on this agenda. Council rules prohibit clapping, booing, or shouts of approval or disagreement from the audience. Clapping, booing, shouting or other actions from the audience which, disturbs, impedes, or otherwise renders infeasible the meeting’s orderly conduct, who, after a request by the presiding officer, refuses to cease such behavior may be removed from the City Council chambers or remote participation platform.

  REGULAR MEETING
  TUESDAY, JANUARY 20, 2026

The City Council of the City of Azusa met in Closed and Regular session at Azusa Auditorium at 213 E.
Foothill Blvd., Azusa, CA 91702.

Mayor Gonzales called the meeting to order at 6:30 P.M.

ROLL CALL: Roll call was taken by City Clerk Cornejo.

PRESENT:  COUNCILMEMBERS: GONZALES, ALVAREZ, AVILA, MENDEZ, BO
ABSENT:  COUNCILMEMBERS: NONE

ALSO PRESENT

Elected Officials: City Clerk Cornejo

Staff Members: City Manager Gonzalez, City Attorney Richman, Economic and Community Development
Director Jimenez, Lieutenant Sears

PUBLIC COMMENT - None

CLOSED SESSION

The City Council recessed to Closed Session at 6:30 p.m. to discuss the following item.

1. CONFERENCE WITH REAL PROPERTY NEGOTIATORS. Pursuant to California Government Code,
  Section 54956.8.
  Property Address: 622-624 North San Gabriel Avenue; APN: 8611-004-912 to 914
  City Negotiator:  Sergio Gonzalez, City Manager
  Negotiating Parties: Luis Nieblas
  Under Negotiation: Price and Terms for Payment
REGULAR SESSION

Mayor Gonzales called the meeting to order at 7:30 P.M.

CEREMONIAL

Swearing in of Mayor Edward J. Alvarez and Mayor Pro Tem Jesse Avila, Jr

Mayor Pro Tem Jesse Avila, Jr. was sworn in by City Clerk Cornejo, accompanied by his nephews, Eli and
Gavin Canizales.

Mayor Edward J. Alvarez was sworn in by City Clerk Cornejo, accompanied by his daughter Julia Alvarez.

Mayor Edward J. Alvarez thanked everyone for coming; expressed his appreciation to his family; stated that it
has been an honor to serve on the City Council for the past 13 years; and noted that the City is doing very well.

City Council Minutes  Page | 1
January 20, 2026
 City Manager Gonzalez announced that the office of Gil Cisneros sent certificates for the new Mayor and
Mayor Pro Tem; and recognized Sandra Armenta Lopez representing the office of Senator Susan Rubio and
Alexis Sanchez representing Assemblymember Blanca Rubio.

ROLL CALL: Roll call was taken by City Clerk Cornejo.

PRESENT: COUNCILMEMBERS:  ALVAREZ, AVILA, GONZALES, MENDEZ, BOW
ABSENT: COUNCILMEMBERS:  NONE

ALSO PRESENT

Elected Officials: City Clerk Cornejo

Staff Members: City Manager Gonzalez, City Attorney Richman, Deputy City Manager DeAnda-Scaia, Chief
of Police Wenrick, Lieutenant Sears, Director of Administrative Services Johnson, Director of Economic &
Community Development Jimenez, Director of Community Resources Carpenter, Director of I.T. Guadagnino,
City Clerk Services Manager Juarez, Planning Manager Vizcarra, Emergency Services Manager Manzano –
Garcia, Economic & Community Development Manager Lopez.

The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Emma Pena.

The Invocation was led by Deacon Mike Flores, St. Francis of Rome Church.

CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Richman reported that Closed Session was conducted and there was no reportable action taken.

CEREMONIAL

Recognition of Gloria Romero

Mayor Alvarez presented a certificate of recognition to Ms. Romero in appreciation of her support of the
Community Resources Department 1st Holiday Teen Party.

Recognition of Azusa Youth Boxing Club

Mayor Alvarez presented Certificates of Recognition to Azusa Youth Boxing Club boxers Robert Lopez,
Joshua Calleja, Justin Calleja and Coach Moe Ferguson.

Mayor Alvarez wished a happy 14th birthday to boxer Joshua Baltera.

PUBLIC PARTICIPATION

Farheen Rizvi, founder of “Human Me, Human Mind Exploration and Expansion,” a local community-based
initiative: expressed appreciation for the support and collaboration provided to coordinate the upcoming
Community Safety and Information Session for the Azusa Mirador community in partnership with the Azusa
Police Department.

Felipe Gamboa, General Manager for Quick Quack Car Wash, announced their plans to open in the next few
weeks; and expressed that they look forward to being part of the community.

REPORTS, UPDATES, AND ANNOUNCEMENTS FROM STAFF/COUNCIL

City Manager Communications

City Manager Sergio Gonzalez reminded the community of the importance of maintaining and clearing
overgrown vegetation to help prevent potential fire hazards; and introduced two new members of the City team:
Alfa Lopez, Economic Development Manager, and Diana Manzano-Garcia, Emergency Services Manager.

City Council Minutes  Page | 2
January 20, 2026
 Councilmember Announcements

Mayor Pro Tem Avila congratulated Mayor Alvarez on his new position; announced the 20th Annual Casino
Night scheduled for February 13; noted that American Legion Post 180 will be celebrating its 100th
anniversary and hosting an event on February 21; and requested that a proclamation recognizing the American
Legion’s 100 years of service be placed on a future City Council agenda.

Councilmember Mendez congratulated Mayor Alvarez and Mayor Pro Tem Avila; noted that he observed that
the roadway striping appears uneven on recently completed Capital Improvement Project along Azusa Avenue
from First Street to Arrow Highway and inquired about available remedies to address the issue. Staff responded
that the project is not considered complete until the Notice of Completion is issued and confirmed that the
concern has been flagged for review.

Councilmember Bow congratulated Mayor Alvarez and Mayor Pro Tem Avila; recognized the City of Azusa’s
first municipal boxing program at Memorial Park; mentioned the 125th anniversary of the Azusa Woman’s
Club; and announced her participation in the commemoration of the Route 66 monument.

Councilmember Gonzales congratulated Mayor Alvarez and Mayor Pro Tem Avila; and suggested a
presentation on Tobacco Retail Licensing (TRL) be scheduled to help educate the Council regarding the sale of
tobacco products in the community.

Mayor Alvarez recognized the new boxing program at Memorial Park; mentioned the new ownership of Sushi
Sawa; and requested that the Azusa Chamber of Commerce reach out to coordinate a future ribbon-cutting
ceremony.

SCHEDULED ITEMS

CONSIDERATION OF A GENERAL PLAN AMENDMENT, ZONE CHANGE, USE PERMIT, MINOR USE
PERMIT, DESIGN REVIEW, TENTATIVE TRACT MAP NO. 84416, TENTATIVE PARCEL MAP. 841740,
AND DEVELOPMENT AGREEMENT NO. GPA/ZC/UP/MUP/DR/TTM/DA-2023-01 FOR 919 SIERRA
MADRE AVENUE (AZUSA GREENS REDEVELOPMENT PROJECT) FOR THE REDEVELOPMENT OF
92.1 ACRES OF A FORMER GOLF COURSE AND ALLOW FOR A 230-UNIT AGE-RESTRICTED
RESIDENTIAL DEVELOPMENT AND SIX INDUSTRIAL BUILDINGS TOTALING 353,075 SQUARE
FEET, INCLUDING REUSE OF AN EXISTING CLUBHOUSE FOR EVENT USE; AND CERTIFICATION
OF FINAL ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT REPORT (SCH NO. 2023120720) AND ADOPTION OF
REQUIRED CEQA FINDINGS, MITIGATION MONITORING AND REPORTING PROGRAM, AND
CONSIDERATION AND ADOPTION OF A STATEMENT OF OVERRIDING CONSIDERATIONS

Planning Manager Vizcarra gave an overview of the Azusa Greens Redevelopment Project, located at 919
Sierra Madre Boulevard; explained that a preliminary project concept was presented to the City Council in
2022, required entitlements were approved in December 2023, and the golf course and restaurant began
operating in 2024.

The proposed General Plan amendment and zone change were presented; it was noted that the Azusa Planning
Commission reviewed the project and voted to recommend that the City Council certify the Environmental
Impact Report (EIR), adopt a Statement of Overriding Considerations, approve the Mitigation Monitoring and
Reporting Program, and approve the project as presented.

Vizcarra also displayed maps of the proposed site plan for both the residential and industrial components of the
development; and discussed the Development Agreement which would have a 10-year term.

Project Manager Fisher of Helix Environmental Planning presented the EIR and gave an overview of the
environmental analysis prepared for the Azusa Greens Redevelopment Project.

Staff responded to questions posed by the Council regarding the inclusion of senior housing within the
development and median income levels associated with the housing component, stating that the senior housing
will double with the new development and discussed anticipated rental price ranges for the proposed units.

The Council requested clarification regarding whether the 230 units were all intended for sale and inquired
about measures in place to prevent golf balls from entering the housing area.

City Council Minutes  Page | 3
January 20, 2026
 Cassiano, Chief Investment Officer for Overton Moore Properties, explained that the poles will be extended and
new netting will be installed to help prevent golf balls from reaching the residential units; and also clarified that
the stacked flats could be available for lease, while the cottages could be offered for sale.

In response to further questions posed by the Council regarding the $4.2 million in off-site improvements
Cassiano explained that the improvements consist of curbs, sidewalks, half-width grind and overlay, and
replacement of water mains.

The Council also inquired about the traffic study that is required once the project reaches 80% occupancy,
specifically requesting clarification on where the funding would come from to install potential traffic signals.
Staff responded that the funding for the signals would come from the City.

Discussion ensued regarding the importance of the golf course to the community and whether there were any
future plans to completely build over the remainder of the course. Cassiano explained that there is no need to do
so, as he views the golf course as a valuable amenity to the Development, and agreed that no redevelopment
projects would take place on the golf course for at least another 50 years.

Mayor Alvarez opened the Public Hearing.

City Clerk Cornejo certified the publication of the Public Hearing in the San Gabriel Valley Tribune on
January 9, 2026; and announced that one correspondence letter from Grace Hollenbrook had been
received and provided to the Council.
Public Comment
